title: Batch + Cache Tuning: Lab Notes and Regression Checklist
content:
Summary:
These are iterative lab notes from a run of experiments designed to map latency / cost / quality tradeoffs across batching, prefix/KV caching, and max_tokens caps for the v1.4 candidate model family (open-llama-derived variant we are evaluating for Hosted). Aim: produce a short checklist + regression signal set that the platform and applied-ml teams can use to recommend default runtime knobs and rollback thresholds for canary rollouts.

Goals and success criteria:
- Find configurations that reduce per-token cost by >=15% vs baseline w/o increasing median latency by >20% or p95 by >10%.
- Confirm cache warmup behavior: cold-start penalty <= 150ms for common short prompts (<=64 tokens) with cache enabled.
- Validate that quality metrics (BLEU/BERTScore/answer-exact-match on our small prompt eval set) degrade by <=1.5% absolute for recommended configs.

Hardware / infra snapshot:
- Test cluster: dev-dedicated-gpu-3 (4xA100-40GB configured as one pool)
- Runtime: serving-runtime@main (commit 8e12f3d) with KV cache implementation A (prefetch-v2)
- Quant variants: fp16 and int8 (quantize-aware conversion pipeline qa/convert-int8@sha:5f1b)

Model + prompt sets used:
- Candidate model tag: rwd-open-llama-v1.4-candidate
- Prompt sets: short-instructions (30k prompts sampled), customer-chat-sim (5k dialogs), long-context-docs (1k multi-turn, 512+ tokens)
- Eval slices: short (<=64), medium (65-256), long (257-1024)

Experiment matrix (not exhaustive):
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8, 16
- Cache: off, prefix-cache-enabled (kv-cache), aggressive-prefetch-enabled
- max_tokens cap: 64, 128, 256, 512
- Quant: fp16, int8
- Routing/queueing: strict latency SLO queue vs throughput queue (we used throughput queue for these runs)

Representative results (median across 10 runs per configuration). Values are synthetic-but-realistic metrics observed in lab. Cost is estimated $ per 1M tokens on Dedicated pool using current unit cost model.

Table (CSV-style):
config_id,batch,cache,max_tokens,quant,median_latency_ms,p95_latency_ms,tokens_per_sec,cost_per_1M_tokens_usd,bertscore_delta
base-fp16-b1-cache-off,1,off,256,fp16,168,402,18.6,24.5,0.0
b1-cache-on-prefetch,1,on,256,fp16,210,430,20.9,20.8,-0.4
b4-cache-on-prefetch,4,on,256,fp16,220,515,61.7,9.1,-0.6
b8-cache-on,8,on,128,fp16,290,720,88.2,6.4,-1.0
b16-cache-on,16,on,128,fp16,510,1250,165.4,3.8,-1.5
b4-int8-cache-on,4,on,256,int8,260,610,94.8,5.5,-1.2
b8-int8-cache-off,8,off,256,int8,430,980,52.0,8.6,-0.9
smallcap-b4-cache-on,4,on,64,fp16,205,470,84.5,11.3,-0.2
smallcap-b8-cache-on,8,on,64,fp16,240,560,126.7,7.2,-0.5

Notes on the numbers above:
- Enabling prefix cache/persistent KV cache improves steady-state throughput and lowers cost per token dramatically for medium/long workloads once cache is warm; cold-start penalty increases median latency (compare base-fp16-b1-cache-off vs b1-cache-on-prefetch).
- Batching trades latency for throughput: batch size 4 with cache on is a good sweet spot for our medium-sliced prompts (roughly 9-12x lower cost per token vs single-request baseline in these tests).
- Very large batches (16) show diminishing returns for cost and increase queueing/P95 substantially; not recommended for latency-sensitive tiers.
- int8 reduces cost further but showed slightly larger BERTScore delta on some QA prompts; worth gating behind a targeted eval set.
- Tight max_tokens caps (64) control tail compute costs for short prompts while preserving quality for short-instruction slices. For chat-like long-context usage, 256 or 512 remains necessary.

Cache warmup behavior and recommendations:
- Warmup sequence observed: first request with cache miss => cold latency spike (~+120-350ms) depending on prompt length; subsequent requests on same prefix show 30-50% latency drop.
- For hosted API defaults consider: cache=on, prefetch=enabled, batch_target=4, max_tokens_default=256 for general use. Offer "low-latency" tier with batch_target=1, cache=on but prefetch=off and stricter CPU-side priority.

Quality regressions and evaluation harness notes:
- Use the existing promptset registry but add a small targeted set (regression-signal-120) focusing on edge-case factual QA and code synthesis which proved sensitive to int8 quantization.
- Thresholds for auto-alert: BERTScore drop >1.0 absolute OR answer-exact-match drop >1.5% across regression-signal-120 triggers an alert and prevents canary escalation.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How to capture multi-tenant interference in Dedicated pools? Our dev pool is single-tenant; need to run smaller noisy neighbor injections to simulate real load (ticketed: AIINF-418).
- Quantization knobs: run mixed-precision (fp16 compute, int8 matmul) path to see if quality holds while retaining int8 cost benefits.
- Should prefix cache be persisted across model rollouts or invalidated on major model version changes? (ops + security implications)

Immediate action items:
- Marco: run targeted int8 QA sweep on regression-signal-120 with mixed-precision variant by 2026-01-22.
- Avery: add cold-start warmup trace to the console dashboard for p50/p95 warmup trendline; link to canary UI (JIRA AIINF-420).
- Samira: create a short customer-facing one-pager describing the latency tiers and recommended defaults for Hosted API docs (due 2026-01-29).

Recommended default knobs (proposal):
- Hosted default: cache=on, prefetch=enabled, batch_target=4, max_tokens=256, quant=fp16
- Low-latency tier: cache=on, prefetch=off, batch_target=1, max_tokens=128, quant=fp16
- Cost-optimized tier (self-serve opt-in): cache=on, prefetch=enabled, batch_target=8, max_tokens=256, quant=int8 (check quality gate)

Appendix: quick run recipe for reproducing the main sweep locally:
- Checkout serving-runtime@8e12f3d and rwd-open-llama-v1.4-candidate artifact from model registry.
- Use perf-script/batch-cache-sweep.sh with flags: --batches 1,4,8,16 --cache on,off --max-tokens 64,128,256 --quant fp16,int8 --repeats 10
- Upload metrics to s3://redwood-ml-lab/batch-cache-sweep/YYYYMMDD/run.json and paste link in the linked_artifacts list.

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts:
- Consider adding a small synthetic "prefix re-use" generator to quantify realistic prefix-hit rates for hosted traffic vs enterprise private deployments.
- Follow up with Platform Eng to expose a per-model default recommended knob set in the model catalog so onboarding can be near-zero config.

End of file.
